title: Proof of the $C_2$ traces on $S^\mu$ and on the regular representation
html:
Proof. Proof of the C_2 traces on S^\mu and on the regular representation

Proof. C_2 is central, so by Schur's lemma [serre1977] it acts on the irreducible S^\mu by a scalar. That scalar is the common eigenvalue of \sum_i L_i^2 on the Gelfand–Tsetlin basis of S^\mu: each L_i acts on a basis vector indexed by a standard tableau T by the content of the cell holding i, so \sum_i L_i^2 acts by \sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2 — the same value for every T, as centrality requires. The restricted operator is therefore \bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\bigr) \cdot \mathrm{id}_{S^\mu}, and the trace of a scalar multiple of the identity is that scalar times the dimension:

  \mathrm{Tr}\bigl(C_2|_{S^\mu}\bigr)
  = \Bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\Bigr)\dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr).

For the regular representation, decompose \mathbb{C}[S_n] by Artin–Wedderburn [sagan2001]: each S^\mu occurs with multiplicity \dim(S^\mu), so

  \mathbb{C}[S_n] \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\mu \vdash n}
    \bigl(S^\mu\bigr)^{\oplus \dim(S^\mu)} .

Trace is additive over that decomposition, and each summand contributes the value just computed, giving

  \mathrm{Tr}(C_2)
  = \sum_{\mu \vdash n}
     \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr) \cdot
     \Bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\Bigr) \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr)
  = \sum_{\mu \vdash n}
     \Bigl(\sum_{\square \in \mu} c(\square)^2\Bigr) \dim\bigl(S^\mu\bigr)^2 .

Dividing by n! = \sum_\mu \dim(S^\mu)^2 turns the right-hand side into the Plancherel expectation \mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{Planch}}\bigl[\sum_\square c(\square)^2\bigr], which is the form Piece B consumes. \blacksquare
